target_claim: Let F be a field of characteristic p>2, let A⊂F be finite, and put n=|A|≤p^(2/3). Let F̄ be an algebraic closure of F and define Q=(AA−AA)/(A+A−A−A)={ (a1a2−a3a4)/(a5+a6−a7−a8) : a1,…,a8∈A and a5+a6−a7−a8≠0 }. For any ξ∈F̄\Q, replace A by the shifted set A+ξ. Equivalently, retaining a,b,c∈A as the unshifted variables, associate to every ordered triple (a,b,c)∈A³ the homogeneous point-coordinate quadruple (a−c:a+ξ:b+ξ:c+ξ) and the dual homogeneous plane-coordinate quadruple (b+ξ:−(c+ξ):c−a:a+ξ), regarded over F̄. A homogeneous quadruple must be nonzero; two point-coordinate quadruples, or two dual plane-coordinate quadruples, define the same projective point or plane exactly when one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other. The claim is that, for every such permitted ξ, all these quadruples are nonzero and each of the two maps from A³ is injective. Thus the construction gives exactly n³ distinct projective points and exactly n³ distinct projective planes.
